title: Tail Recursion and the Stack Overflow Problem
description: A tail-recursive count-down function that should run in constant space in Scheme, but would crash a naive Python evaluator with 10000 recursive calls. The trampoline technique converts tail calls into iteration.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Line 1 defines count-down as a lambda taking n. The function counts down from n to 0.

The body is an if: if (= n 0) returns 'done, else tail-calls (count-down (- n 1)). The recursive call is in tail position  -  it's the last thing the function does, so no stack frame is needed after it.

steps.question: Line 6 calls (count-down 10000). In a proper Scheme implementation this runs in constant stack space. In our naive Python evaluator from Model 3, what happens and why?
steps.answer: The Python evaluator's scheme_eval recurses for every Scheme call, even tail calls. Each recursive call to count-down adds a Python stack frame. At 10000 calls it exceeds Python's recursion limit and raises RecursionError. The Scheme semantics guarantee tail calls use no stack, but the Python implementation doesn't honor that.

steps.description: The call (count-down 10000) should return 'done after 10000 tail-recursive steps. In a TCO evaluator it loops 10000 times with constant Python stack. The trampoline technique makes this work.
Run it. (define count-down ...) creates a Procedure with params=['n'], body=if..., env=global. Binds count-down in global env.

(count-down 10000): looks up count-down, calls Procedure with n=10000. In TCO evaluator: while loop updates x=body, env=call_env, continues. Each iteration: n decreases by 1. At n=0, returns 'done. Output: done.
